ideas: Their influence on young people's spending and values
Lack of regulation around paid promotions
Positive uses, like raising awareness of causes

phrases.meaning: posts that a company pays for
help people know about an issue
receiving a lot of public attention

model: It seems to me that some influencers do have too much power, mainly because their influence isn't really regulated. Top influencers have a loyal fan base of millions, and many of those followers are impressionable young people who tend to trust them more than traditional advertising. When an influencer promotes a product, it doesn't always look like sponsored content, so fans don't realise they're being sold something. Last year my younger cousin bought an expensive skincare set only because her favourite TikToker recommended it, and it gave her a rash. Influencers can also create unrealistic expectations about bodies and lifestyles. Having said that, I wouldn't say all of this power is harmful. Many influencers use their time in the spotlight to raise awareness of important issues, like mental health or plastic waste, and some have raised huge amounts for charity. And to some extent, their power comes from the audience, so it's arguably our choice to follow them. Still, I'd say clearer rules on advertising would stop them from swaying public opinion unfairly.
